subject: Temporary SLA adjustment request — Model 3a latency spike and rollback conditions
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@paywise.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Model 3a — sudden p95 latency spike (SLA impact)

Neha,

We started seeing a sustained p95 latency increase for our production traffic to model "3a" starting ~08:45 PDT. The Dashboard shows p95 jump from ~180ms to ~420ms for the last 90 minutes, and it has tripped our internal SLO alerts. Our contract (section 4.2) has a 99.9% availability / latency SLO tied to the model variants you host.

This is material for our team — we need confirmation whether this is a regression on Redwood's side or something on our end. Can you confirm:
- Whether any model version rollouts or infra changes occurred around 08:30–09:00?
- Whether there is an automated rollback trigger we should expect (and if credits will be applied if the SLA is missed)?

We are copying procurement because we may need to discuss credits if this is a platform issue.

Please escalate — we rely on 3a for latency-sensitive inference.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Platform Reliability
Paywise Inc.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@paywise.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-20T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model 3a — sudden p95 latency spike (SLA impact)

Samir — thanks for the heads up and very sorry for the disruption. I'm escalating now. High-level: we rolled a minor runtime optimization to the 3a lineage early this morning (v3a.2) but it passed standard perf tests; we are treating this as a priority regression.

Immediate actions:
- Engineering (Priyom, Marcus) are triaging now and will confirm rollback/fallback options within the hour.
- I will request a temporary exception to SLA crediting while we investigate — we want to avoid noisy automatic credits if an automated rollback/fix is about to resolve the issue within a short window.

Can you confirm the timeframe of the spike you observed (start/stop) and whether you saw any error rates increase or only latency? That will help prioritize.

I'll follow up with a recommended mitigation plan in the next update.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-20T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Model 3a — sudden p95 latency spike (SLA impact)

Marcus, Priyom — forwarding Paywise's report. Please:
1) Confirm if v3a.2 deployment was associated with any kernel/scheduler changes that could cause p95 regressions at seq len ~1024.
2) Assess time-to-rollback to v3a.1 and whether we can do an automated or manual rollback without violating customer-specific routing.
3) If a rollback is imminent, I will request a temporary waiver for SLA credits for an incident window while the rollback is performed.

Goal: resolve within a 3–6 hour window and avoid large credit exposure.

Thanks — Neha

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Model 3a — sudden p95 latency spike (SLA impact)

Quick summary from triage (10:15–11:00):
- Root cause: v3a.2 introduced a new attention-kernel selector path optimized for small sequences; under certain sequence-length distributions (we see this at Paywise) it triggers a suboptimal kernel for long inputs (>=512 tokens), causing context copy thrashing and higher per-token latency.
- Observed impact (Paywise production window): p50 ~210ms, p95 ~420–460ms, p99 tails ~820ms. No increase in 5xx errors — pure latency regression.
- Rollback impact: Rolling back to v3a.1 reduces p95 back to ~180ms in our staging repro. Estimated safe window to rollback with no routing disruption: 12–18 minutes (we will drain in-flight requests and switch routing).

Proposed immediate mitigations:
A) Manual rollback to v3a.1 (recommended) — target T+30–45 minutes after approval; will require brief routing cutover (12–18m).
B) Pin Paywise traffic to a compatibility variant (3a-compat) for the next 24h while we push a proper fix in 3.1.1. That avoids a global rollback.
C) Telemetry: attaching latency_dashboard.png and kernel_trace.txt from the repro run.

Next steps I need from you (Neha):
- Authorization to perform manual rollback OR approval to pin traffic.
- Confirmation you want us to request a temporary SLA exception/credit waiver while we perform the rollback.

I'll be standing by to execute as soon as we have the green light.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@paywise.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, procurement@paywise.com
Date: 2026-07-20T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed temporary SLA adjustment & mitigation plan (Model 3a)

Samir — thanks for patience. Engineering confirmed the regression tied to v3a.2. Summary and proposal below.

Observed impact:
- Start: ~2026-07-20T08:45 PDT; p95 rose to 420–460ms (no error-rate increase).
- Root cause: kernel selector regression in v3a.2 for longer sequences.

Proposed immediate plan (we recommend A or B):
A) Manual rollback to v3a.1 (recommended):
   - ETA: rollback start within 30–45 minutes from approval; cutover 12–18m.
   - Expected result: p95 back to ~180ms.
B) Traffic pinning to 3a-compat for Paywise only:
   - ETA: immediate (5–10m) to pin routing, 24h duration, then revert when fix is deployed.

SLA handling: to avoid noisy auto-crediting while we execute the fix, Redwood requests a temporary SLA adjustment for the incident window (2026-07-20T08:45–2026-07-20T14:00 PDT). Specifically: Redwood requests a one-off waiver of formal credit calculations for claims tied solely to this incident period provided we complete rollback/pinning and validation within 24 hours and produce a post-incident report.

Attachments: latency_dashboard.png (before/after), kernel_trace.txt. I have also attached a short form request document (req_for_sla_adjustment.docx) for legal/commercial.

If Paywise approves either A or B, we will proceed immediately and follow up with a detailed timeline and postmortem. If Paywise prefers to retain automatic credit calculations, we will still proceed with rollback but understand credits will be applied per contract.

Please reply with the option you prefer (A/B) and whether procurement needs any different paperwork.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0193

From: Samir Patel <samir@paywise.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-07-21T16:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed temporary SLA adjustment & mitigation plan (Model 3a)

Neha — appreciate the quick triage and clear options. Paywise will accept option A (manual rollback to v3a.1) and grant Redwood the requested temporary adjustment for the incident window, provided we receive:
- Confirmation of the rollback schedule (exact UTC timestamps) 30 minutes before execution
- Post-rollback validation (p95 graphs and sample traces)
- The SLA waiver documented (Procurement will review the attached docx and sign a short amendment)

Procurement (cc'd) will coordinate the signature. Please send the DocuSign link when ready, and confirm the rollback time.

Thanks again — Samir
Head of Platform Reliability
Paywise Inc.
